componentPlan.focusQuote: A glider is a special kind of aircraft that has no engine.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Checks basic glider facts and steady descent ideas before calculations
Explores tangent relation between height distance and glide angle for testing

overview.headline: Steady glider descent links glide angle lift and drag

keyPoints.point: Steady descent holds constant velocity with no acceleration while losing altitude as it travels
keyPoints.quote: If a glider is in a steady (constant velocity and no acceleration) descent, it loses altitude as it travels.

keyPoints.point: Flight path meets ground at glide angle found from distance flown and altitude change
keyPoints.quote: The flight path intersects the ground at an angle a called the glide angle.

keyPoints.point: Tangent of glide angle equals height change divided by distance flown for calculation
keyPoints.quote: The tangent tan of the glide angle a is equal to the change in height h divided by the distance flown d:

keyPoints.point: Lift and drag balance weight with sine and cosine parts of glide angle in steady glide
keyPoints.quote: The lift times the sine of the glide angle is equal to the drag times the cosine of the glide angle.

keyTerms.gloss: aircraft with no engine studied with toy models
